clue.text: Duck with drink trouble?

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of beer, a drink
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone is having a hard time with their drinking, or a duck is struggling to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' reads as a verb or a term of endearment, but it is the bird being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintail is a species of dabbling duck with a long pointed tail.

clue.text: Claim to be through with love - isn't that laying it on a bit thick?

definitions.text: laying it on a bit thick
definitions.note: the definition describes the technique; the answer names it

blocks.note: 'I'm' is what you say to claim to be something
through as in finished, over and done with
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be over a romance, and is accused of overdoing the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPASTO is paint applied so thickly that brush or knife marks stand out; the idiom 'laying it on thick' doubles as the painting description.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of applying pigment in heavy, raised layers on the canvas.

clue.text: Can't he take the part of a Greek character?

indicators.note: taking part of the preceding words means lifting a run of letters from inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the end of can't, all of he and the start of take

explanation.surface: An actor is asked whether he can't play the role of someone from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the T of can't through HE into the start of take.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character in that writing system.

clue.text: Starting with a capital letter, usually

blocks.note: first meaning: occurring at the beginning, first
second meaning: the first letter of a name, normally written as a capital

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one style rule about beginning a sentence; it splits after 'Starting'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means first or opening; as a noun it is the first letter of someone's name, typically written in upper case.

clue.text: One, for example, turning to group for cover

indicators.note: turning round sends the abbreviation just before it the other way

blocks.note: a band is a group of people or musicians
a means one
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Someone, as an instance, turns to a group seeking protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse clue order: BAND, then A, then GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used to cover and protect a wound.

clue.text: One with clove-hitch in shady retreat

indicators.note: a hitch is a jerk or a snag, something that disturbs the letters next to it

blocks.note: a means one
the five letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor tying a clove hitch sits in a shady nook.
explanation.walkthrough: A clove hitch is a common sailing knot, so the hyphenated phrase looks like a single item; it splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess or sheltered nook, a secluded spot set back from a room or garden.

clue.text: The cleaner has put a chap off

blocks.note: with 'off' at the end of the clue, 'put off' means discourage
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: The office cleaner has scared off some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put ... off' wraps round 'a chap', but the pieces simply join: deter a gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, a substance used to wash things.

clue.text: Keeps airman from flying for good reasons

blocks.note: first meaning: stops a pilot taking off, as a verb
second meaning: justification

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about an airman banned for valid reasons; it splits at 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ground a pilot is to forbid them to fly; grounds also means a basis or justification for an action.

clue.text: Exaggeration about summary of financial position

blocks.note: over as in 'arguing over', concerning
a bank statement summarises an account's position

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of hyping a set of company accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An overstatement claims more than is true, which is what exaggerating means.

clue.text: Some cheap seats placed in recess

indicators.note: 'some' takes only a portion of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddling the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: Budget seating has been put in an alcove of a theatre or church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Appeal for supernatural aid in one's business

blocks.note: taken as written
a vocation is one's calling or occupation

explanation.surface: A witch or priest calls on the spirits as part of the job.
explanation.definitionFit: An invocation is a prayer or summons calling on a god or spirit for help.

clue.text: Soldier has to enquire about air

indicators.note: about as in moved around, so the letters of the next word are stirred up

blocks.note: to ask is to enquire
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier must ask about the atmosphere, or a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: An askari was a local soldier serving a European colonial power in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Askari is the Swahili-derived word for an East African soldier or police officer.

clue.text: Tear about always, but not disrespectful

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the next

blocks.note: a rent is a tear or rip in cloth
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Someone is always rushing around, yet never rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' suggests rushing, but here it is a rip in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means deeply respectful, the opposite of being disrespectful.

clue.text: Establish correspondence, later suffering change in heart

indicators.note: a word undergoing change has its letters rearranged
in places the altered word inside the next piece

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Pen pals start writing, but one later has a change of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To correlate is to show a mutual relationship or connection between things.

clue.text: Enlisted soldiers performed crude rite

indicators.note: a rite that is performed is acted out, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Army conscripts go through a rough initiation ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit is to sign up new members, so recruited means took troops into service.

clue.text: Figures point to being strained

blocks.note: tens are numbers, figures
E for east, a compass point

explanation.surface: The numbers suggest that something is under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means stretched tight or nervously anxious, both senses of strained.

clue.text: Stiff person in jam

blocks.note: first meaning: a dull or rigid individual
second meaning: to become fixed and unable to move

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rigid person in trouble; 'in' links two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbending or boring person is called a stick, and to stick is to become jammed or wedged fast.

clue.text: Rome shattered by explosive shell, causing distress

indicators.note: something shattered is broken in pieces, so the city's name is broken up
a shell forms the outside casing round the broken letters

blocks.note: TNT is a common explosive
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Rome is devastated by bombardment, and its people suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe physical or mental suffering, a stronger word for anguish.

clue.text: Binding criticism

blocks.note: first meaning: a restriction or constriction, something that ties
second meaning: a censorious remark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding criticism' reads as one phrase, like a verdict that must be obeyed; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a limit or restraint, and also a severe critical remark, usually in the plural.

clue.text: Cut inside out, including first chapter

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the word before is jumbled
first asks for only the opening letter of the next word
including means taking something inside

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
the initial letter of this word

explanation.surface: An editor cuts the inside pages, including the opening chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Incised means engraved or slit, carved into a surface with a sharp blade.

clue.text: Provide a substitute for two materials

blocks.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
lace is an openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A tailor swaps in two kinds of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Rep (or repp) is a ribbed upholstery fabric; lace is the second material.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace something is to put another thing in its place, swapping it out.

clue.text: Counterfeit article by priest

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A forged object has been made by a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spiritual healer or medicine man, a kind of tribal holy figure.

clue.text: Vehicle in which fairy queen returned with hooligan aboard

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the name is read from right to left
aboard means on board, carried inside

blocks.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, in Romeo and Juliet
a rough is a violent lout

explanation.surface: A fairy monarch rides home in a carriage with a thug on board.
explanation.walkthrough: MAB reversed is BAM, which holds ROUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with an enclosed body.

clue.text: Article about facsimile cover for bed

indicators.note: about here pairs the two items so that one sits around the other

blocks.note: a facsimile is an exact copy
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news piece concerns a fax of a bedspread design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' usually puts the first item outside, but here the article sits inside the facsimile.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a cloth covering hung above a four-poster bed.

clue.text: Artless one in ecclesiastical passage

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the passage that follows

blocks.note: the nave is the central aisle of a church
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated person stands in a church aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and unworldly, lacking guile or cunning.

clue.text: Feelings of people involved in sin test?

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of the last words are twisted
in sets the people inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: seven letters rearranged
men are people

explanation.surface: People taking a moral examination have strong emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiments are emotional attitudes or views, the things one feels about something.

clue.text: Country one managed to see

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A traveller succeeded in visiting a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in the Middle East, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Undergraduate makes boss throw out ten

indicators.note: to throw something out of order is to scramble it

blocks.note: a stud is a raised boss or knob
three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A university student gets the manager to dismiss ten staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a manager but a round raised stud, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is someone studying at university for a first degree.

clue.text: Stuck at this point in total

indicators.note: in sets the first phrase inside the word that follows

blocks.note: to total is to add up
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Someone stuck to a position at this stage of the calculation.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhered is the past tense of adhere, meaning clung or remained attached.
